scenes.name: Divas funky
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: Pocas instrumentistas, pero divas que no cedían terreno, casi siempre sin una banda como la de Chaka. James Brown reclutó a Vicki Anderson, Marva Whitney y Lyn Collins; Yvonne Fair hizo The Bitch Is Black en Motown; Millie Jackson construyó tres décadas de descaro; Betty Davis, exmujer de Miles (a quien descubrió a Hendrix y la ropa freak), grabó tres discos de funk ardiente demasiado calientes para Estados Unidos. Clinton fichó a Jessica Cleaves y a las coristas de Sly, Lynn Mabry y Dawn Silva, primeras Brides of Funkenstein («Disco to Go»). Las Pointer Sisters («Yes We Can Can») y LaBelle (Patti LaBelle, Nona Hendryx, Sarah Dash; «Lady Marmalade»), ambas con Allen Toussaint; Tina Turner aguantó a Ike. Demasiadas acabaron al frente de grupos de disco fantasma.
scenes.family: Soul y proto-funk: Stax, Nueva Orleans, Motown

podcast.title: Prolific Songwriter and Producer
podcast.body: A "New Orleanian legend," Allen Toussaint wrote "Yes We Can," originally recorded by Lee Dorsey in 1970, and produced LaBelle's smash hit "Lady Marmalade." He also wrote "Happiness" for The Pointer Sisters, showcasing his diverse contributions to music. "The song was written by his fellow New Orliniian legend, Alan Tussaint."
